name: Broccoli & cheese bake (פשטידת ברוקולי וגבינות)

source.author: Hebrew recipe (pasted)
source.notes: Baked broccoli-and-cheese pashtida: 600 g frozen broccoli + a cottage/white/Bulgarian cheese + egg custard, bound with a little flour/cornflour/baking powder, topped with panko + yellow cheese for crunch. Analyzed for the whole bake; per_serving = batch ÷ 8 (~170 g each). Cheeses taken at the stated 5% versions. Estimate. Optimization captured in suggested_mods — an optimized variant is in chat.

serving_desc: ≈170 g slice (batch ÷8) — side or light main; 2 slices = a fuller meal

ingredients.note: drain VERY well after cooking — wet broccoli = watery bake
salty — it sets the salt level; verify pasteurized (her note)
swap to whole spelt for fiber (see mods)
depends on how salty the Bulgarian is — taste first
whole-wheat panko adds a little fiber

steps: Soften the broccoli in boiling salted water a few minutes; drain well and cool. Keep a few nice florets aside, roughly chop the rest.
Sauté the onion in olive oil until soft and lightly golden; add garlic ~30 sec.
Mix cottage, white cheese, Bulgarian, eggs, flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt and pepper.
Fold in the broccoli and the sautéed onion.
Transfer to a dish, level it, top with the reserved florets, a little yellow cheese, an even layer of panko, and a few sprays of oil.
Bake 180 °C top-bottom 45–55 min until set and golden. Rest 10–15 min before slicing.

batch_totals.note: Whole bake (8 slices). Broccoli drives the fiber + folate + vitamin C; the cheeses + eggs drive protein + calcium. Sodium is high (Bulgarian + added salt + baking powder) and the flour/cornflour/panko are the refined-carb bits — both are the main optimization levers.

him.verdict: A genuinely strong veggie bake — for only ~175 kcal a slice it packs ~12.8 g protein (~7.4 g protein per 100 kcal, excellent for a vegetable dish) from the cottage/white/Bulgarian cheeses + eggs, plus real fiber and a big folate/vitamin-C load from 600 g of broccoli. Fat is moderate and mostly from the eggs + cheese. The only soft spots: sodium is high (Bulgarian + added salt), and the flour/cornflour/panko add a little refined carb. Dial those two and it's a 9 — see the optimized version.
flags: ~12.8 g protein / 175 kcal slice (~7.4 g protein per 100 kcal)
high sodium (~425 mg/slice; ~3,400 mg batch) — Bulgarian + added salt
refined carbs from flour + cornflour + panko topping
moderate fat (~7.4 g/slice), mostly eggs + cheese
suggested_mods: Skip the added salt — the Bulgarian is already salty (taste the mix first)
Swap the 3 tbsp flour to whole spelt and use whole-wheat panko — more fiber, whole-grain
Halve the yellow-cheese topping (~15 g) — panko alone crisps up with a spray of oil; trims fat + sodium
Add 1–2 egg whites to push protein further with no extra fat
Great as a protein+veg anchor; pair with a lean protein (chicken) to make it a full cut meal

her_preconception.verdict: An excellent preconception dish — close to ideal for her lens. 600 g of broccoli makes it a folate powerhouse (her #1 nutrient), the 3 eggs bring choline (fetal brain development), the cheeses add calcium + protein, and the broccoli's own vitamin C helps iron absorption. Fully baked and set. One thing to confirm: the Bulgarian cheese is a brined soft cheese — it's baked through here (cooked = considered safe) and the 'refined' Israeli ones are usually pasteurized, but verify it. This is a dish worth making for her regularly.
prenatal_highlights: folate from 600 g broccoli — her top preconception nutrient
choline from 3 eggs; vitamin C (broccoli) aids iron absorption
calcium + protein from the cheeses; high fiber; fully baked

safety_advisories.note: Bulgarian cheese is a brined soft cheese — Listeria risk unless pasteurized. It's baked through here (considered safe cooked) and refined Israeli Bulgarit is usually pasteurized; verify it.
safety_advisories.swap: verify pasteurized / keep it baked through, or use a little extra white cheese

suggested_mods: Verify the Bulgarian is pasteurized (it's cooked here, so low risk)
Already rich in folate — no changes needed for her; the lower-sodium tweaks help too

cooking_guide: Cook the frozen broccoli in boiling salted water just a few minutes — don't overcook it to mush. Then DRAIN IT VERY WELL and even press/pat out the excess water: wet broccoli is the #1 cause of a soggy pashtida. Reserve a few nice florets for the top and roughly chop the rest.
Sauté the chopped onion in the olive oil over medium until soft and lightly golden (this builds sweetness), then add the garlic for ~30 sec — don't let it brown or it turns bitter.

In a bowl, whisk the eggs, then stir in the cottage, white cheese and crumbled Bulgarian with the flour, cornflour, baking powder and pepper. Go EASY on the salt — taste the mix first, because the Bulgarian is already salty.
Fold in the well-drained broccoli and the sautéed onion until evenly coated.

Transfer to a greased/lined baking dish and level the top. Arrange the reserved florets on top, scatter a little yellow cheese, then an even layer of panko, and a few sprays of oil — the panko + oil is what gives the crisp golden crust without deep-frying.

Bake at 180 °C (conventional, top-bottom heat) 45–55 min until the center is set (not wobbly) and the top is deep golden. A knife in the middle should come out clean. Larger/wider dish = check earlier.
REST 10–15 min before cutting — this is important: it lets the custard finish setting so the slices hold together instead of falling apart.
Tips: for more fiber use whole-spelt flour + whole-wheat panko; for more protein add 1–2 egg whites; a grating of nutmeg or a little chili lifts the flavor.
